definitions.explanation: A thoroughly bad or wicked person. Someone who commits evil deeds or engages in criminal or immoral behavior. Stronger than mere mischief — implies genuine malice or villainy.

examples.japanese: あいつは{悪党|あくとう}だ。
{悪党|あくとう}どもがこの{町|まち}を{支配|しはい}している。
examples.english: A gang of villains controls this town.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{見|み}た{目|め}は{紳士|しんし}だが、{裏|うら}では{悪党|あくとう}として{知|し}られていた。
examples.english: He looked like a gentleman, but behind the scenes he was known as a scoundrel.

notes:
USAGE:
{悪党|あくとう} refers to a genuinely bad or evil person. It is commonly used in fiction, historical dramas, and storytelling. In everyday speech, it carries a strong negative judgment.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大|おお}{悪党|あくとう}: a great villain, arch-villain
- {悪党|あくとう}の{一味|いちみ}: a gang of villains
- {悪党|あくとう}{面|づら}: a villainous face

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {悪党|あくとう}: villain, scoundrel (genuine evil or criminality)
- {悪者|わるもの}: bad guy (broader, milder — includes petty wrongdoers)
- {悪人|あくにん}: evil person (literary, emphasizes moral wickedness)
